title: Does combining activation-based detection with a lightweight keyword filter outperform either alone?

original_idea.problem: A simple ensemble of activation probe + keyword filter has not been evaluated against either standalone approach on a diverse benchmark.
original_idea.direction: Implement three detectors (probe, keyword filter, OR-ensemble). Evaluate on JailbreakBench with 5 attack types. Measure AUROC, precision, recall, FPR.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Ensembles may achieve better coverage at minimal cost.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: ensemble coverage improvement -> practical low-cost production baseline. But the safety impact is incremental (combining known approaches) rather than revealing a new mechanism or addressing a critical gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Both keyword filtering and linear probing are computationally trivial. OR-ensemble is a simple logical combination. Beginners can implement all three components with standard tools.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a comparison table across 3 detectors and 5 attack types. Clear methodology. Components are independently testable.

novelty.reasoning: Ensemble detection approaches are conceptually well-known, and content filtering systems already use ensembles of classification models. The idea of combining a lightweight detector with a more sophisticated one as a two-stage pipeline is mentioned in recent work (e.g., concept-based triage + full analysis). However, the specific combination of an activation linear probe with a keyword filter evaluated head-to-head on JailbreakBench across 5 attack types with precision/recall/FPR reporting has not been published. The contribution is incremental (combining known approaches) but the systematic evaluation would fill a practical gap.

evidence: LLM Jailbreak Detection for (Almost) Free! EMNLP 2025 Findings. arXiv:2509.14558.
JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking LLMs. NeurIPS 2024.
Recursive Language Models for Jailbreak Detection. arXiv:2602.16520, 2026.
